source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 24 MW of IT capacity, one of only 25 power figures available across 330 mapped Virginia data centers.

The disclosure gap is the story. Virginia has 330 mapped facilities and 25 published power figures, so any state total rests on a small sample. Those 25 facilities account for 1,603 MW of announced capacity, and Sterling's 24 MW is 1.5% of it, ranking 17th. The campus occupies 154,230 square feet of technical space, which is a large footprint for the power it publishes. No certifications are listed.

For AI specifically, capacity in megawatts sets the ceiling on what a site can run, but density sets what it can run efficiently. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, 24 MW corresponds to roughly 600 racks, though that is an assumption about density rather than a published specification. The operator does not disclose whether the campus accepts high-density compute, so its relevance to AI training cannot be settled from these facts.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. It says nothing about grid headroom in Northern Virginia, nothing about power available to expand beyond 24 MW, and nothing about announced expansion, which is the one input the suitability scoring records as missing. A 24 MW figure describes a facility as it stands, not the constraint it will meet.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
